question.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -8 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 3\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{22}=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -8 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ -5 & 15 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{31}=-5,{u}_{22}=4,$ and ${l}_{31}\cdot {u}_{22}=-20.$
